data.reason: The KPI's main goal is town-wide on_time_deliveries (K1). Option 1 raises on-time from 223.8 to 225.0 (+1.2), but only 2/5 seeds improve, so the main-goal gain is not established and may be noise. Its watched-goal gains are large on average: p95_wait_s 110 -> 93.0, max_wait_s 201 -> 129, and late 4.2 -> 3.0. However, these have not been checked per seed, and the current service is already good (lowest on-time rate 0.97, unfinished 0.0). The cost is concrete. C's utility would fall from 56.3 to 40.1, and C votes no. This would be a second consecutive override of C, after the D1 loss (28.8 to 19.0), and the mitigation promised in D1 is still not in place. Road violations would also rise again, from 28.0 to 29.8, and the cause of the earlier rise in D1 has not been examined. In D1 the override was justified by a clear main-goal gain of +9.2 on 5/5 seeds. That justification is missing here. I therefore follow the LLM's recommendation and do not override C's vote on uncertain evidence. A and B vote yes, and B gives up about 8.7 utility, but a majority vote alone does not justify a large repeated loss to one company when the KPI gain is unproven. No contract change is involved, so customers' promised times are unaffected. They keep the current service, but miss a possible reduction in tail waits. That reduction is the main reason to revisit option 1 once per-seed wait data and a mitigation for C are available. I take responsibility for this decision on behalf of the operator.
assumptions: The 5-seed measurements represent next period's conditions (normal + rush).
Staying at v2 (block_k 2) keeps metrics near the current values: on-time 223.8, late 4.2, p95_wait_s 110, max_wait_s 201.
The road violations at 28.0 are not an immediate safety hazard, since v2 passed the constitution.
Option 1 is revertible and can be re-proposed later without loss.
unknowns: Whether the p95_wait_s and max_wait_s improvements under option 1 hold on each seed.
Why C loses so much under faster eviction, and whether a mitigation exists that C would accept.
The cause and safety relevance of the road violations (25.8 -> 28.0 under v2, 29.8 under option 1).
Whether more seeds would show a real main-goal effect for block_k 1.
How customers value shorter tail waits relative to the current service level.
Next period's demand and how the effect of block_k changes under higher load.
